title: Śnieżka and Glacial Cirques
lead: A park on the Polish-Czech border. Śnieżka, Snowy Cirques, Samotnia, and waterfalls falling from granite walls.
body:
A Park on the Border

Karkonosze National Park is one of the oldest national parks in Poland — established in 1959, but protecting an area that had been protected since the 19th century. It lies on the Polish-Czech border, covering the Polish part of the Karkonosze — the highest range of the Sudetes.

The symbol of the park is Śnieżka (1,603 m) — the highest peak of the Karkonosze and the entire Sudetes. At the summit there is a meteorological observatory, the Chapel of St. Lawrence, and a mountain hut where you can rest after the climb. Śnieżka is one of the windiest places in Europe — the wind can blow here at over 200 km/h.

Snowy Cirques and Samotnia

The Karkonosze are famous for their glacial cirques — large depressions in the mountain slopes formed during the Ice Age. The most famous are the Snowy Cirques and the Cirque of Mały Staw, where the Samotnia mountain hut is located — one of the most beautifully situated huts in Poland.

The park offers many trails — from easy walks to demanding hikes. It is worth planning the route to see as much as possible — the Karkonosze are beautiful in every season, but especially in autumn, when the forests turn gold and red.
tip: Check the weather forecast before setting out for Śnieżka. The Karkonosze are one of the windiest places in Europe — the wind can prevent you from reaching the summit.
